quote: immediately gives me pause. You said that, power would be, provided by you guys primarily
stewart_read: Customer directly names a trust wobble caused by the rep's own imprecise phrasing, not by an objection they brought in. This is a self-inflicted credibility cost from unclear language about the grid relationship, not a customer resistance pattern.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as ordinary customer due-diligence rather than a real trust cost, but the customer's word 'immediately gives me pause' is explicit enough to treat as a genuine wobble.
coaching_implication: Coach Carter to lead with a crisp, rehearsed one-line explanation of the grid relationship ('You stay connected to Dominion, but your home draws its own solar power first') before the customer has to ask — precision here prevents the pause entirely.

quote: How much panels can you fit in 10 by 23?
stewart_read: This is the first clean opportunity to deploy the escape hatch ('that's exactly what our design team maps out on-site'), but the rep stays engaged in the roof-math conversation for three more exchanges instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep genuinely didn't recognize the redirect point. Strategic read (rejected): there's no evidence the rep was deliberately letting the customer talk through it as a rapport tactic — the later admission of not knowing suggests the rep was simply behind, not steering.
coaching_implication: Train Carter to recognize the first specific technical spec question as the trigger point for the escape hatch, not the third or fourth.

quote: I'd love to just get your utility bill so we know how many panels you would need, and then just send it over to my design team.
stewart_read: This is the correct move — the rep disengages from a technical debate he cannot win and redirects to the right data point (utility bill/usage) and the right owner (design team), matching the schema's universal escape hatch almost verbatim. It is the single cleanest structural recovery in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as a missed bill-pain anchor opportunity since the rep asks for the bill purely as a design input rather than reflecting the number back as a curiosity hook — that secondary miss is real but does not outweigh the primary value of the scope-discipline redirect itself.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this move by name with Carter — this is the escape hatch working as designed. Secondary layer: coach him to also ask 'do you know roughly what you're paying now?' in the same breath, so the bill becomes an anchor, not just a design input.

quote: Yeah. So it'll take me two months to get that to you.
stewart_read: Customer reveals they haven't moved in and won't have usage data for a month — the rep pivots practically to square footage, but never re-anchors the customer's motivation or creates forward-pulling curiosity about savings once the home is occupied.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read fits best here — there is no signal the rep was deliberately deferring curiosity-building to the closer; the rep simply moved to the next logistical fact (square footage) without commentary.
coaching_implication: Coach Carter to briefly reflect the number back even when it's unavailable now — e.g., naming that the design team will size it once he's in and using power, tying the appointment to seeing his real numbers.

quote: one of the main requirements for getting solar is having a credit score above 650. Is that gonna be an issue for you?
stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the threshold, which is a documented schema drift — the schema's stated threshold is 670. This matches a prior observed drift instance (SESSION18_fcbf33c1) and suggests a floor-wide inconsistency, not a one-off error.
coaching_implication: Flag for reconciliation with Kenny — is 650 or 670 the current active number? If reps are inconsistent, customers could be qualified or DQ'd incorrectly.

quote: Would morning time or afternoon time be better for you?
stewart_read: Rep books a day and time but never runs the full button-up sequence — no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction, no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as acceptable compression given the call's already-long technical detour, but the schema treats these elements as required regardless of call length.
coaching_implication: Drill the full button-up checklist as a fixed close, especially on calls that ran long and technical — the no-show risk is highest exactly when the setter is eager to wrap up.
